summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science degree: discrete mathematics (sets, counting, induction, modular arithmetic, gcd and primes), calculus and a first linear algebra course (matrix rank and row reduction), an algorithms course (asymptotic notations, recurrences, sorting, schoolbook arithmetic), and a theory course on Turing machines and their running time. Complex numbers are known through polar form and roots of unity, and binary and two's-complement representation through computer organization. Each subject is taken only to first-course depth: no abstract algebra beyond the fields and rings that linear algebra uses, no Fourier analysis beyond the finite transform, no number theory beyond gcd, primes and modular inverses, and nothing from coding theory, circuit complexity or the specialist finite-network material.

known.name: Arithmetic modulo n
known.gloss: Integers taken modulo n, where two integers are congruent when they differ by a multiple of n, with addition and multiplication of residues and inverses of residues coprime to n.

known.name: The field with two elements
known.gloss: The set {0, 1} with addition given by exclusive or and multiplication given by AND, so that bit strings are vectors over this field.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
known.gloss: The largest common divisor of two integers, computed by Euclid's algorithm, which also yields integers x and y with ax + by = gcd(a, b) (the extended Euclidean algorithm).

known.name: Prime numbers and trial division
known.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than one with no divisors other than one and itself, and primality of an integer can be decided by testing divisors up to its square root.

known.name: Positional (radix) number representation
known.gloss: Every nonnegative integer has a unique expansion as a sum of digits times powers of a base b, and in base 2 this gives a bit string, written with leading zeros to a fixed width when needed.

known.name: Two's-complement integers
known.gloss: A signed k-bit integer whose leading bit has weight minus 2^(k-1), so that negation is bitwise complement followed by adding one.

known.name: Bitwise operations
known.gloss: Operations on bit strings applied position by position, namely AND, OR, exclusive or, and shifts or cyclic rotations of the string.

known.name: Hamming weight
aliases: Hamming weight of a bit string
known.gloss: The Hamming weight of a binary vector is the number of its entries equal to one, and its parity is that number taken modulo two.

known.name: Floor, ceiling, logarithms and exponentials
known.gloss: The floor and ceiling functions round a real number down or up to an integer, the logarithm inverts the exponential, and elementary inequalities such as 1 + x <= e^x and Bernoulli's inequality are used freely.

known.name: Theta, Omega and little-o notation
known.gloss: f = Theta(g) means f is both O(g) and Omega(g), f = Omega(g) means f is at least a constant times g for all large inputs, and f = o(g) means f/g tends to zero.

known.name: Geometric series
aliases: sum of powers of a ratio
known.gloss: The finite sum of the powers 1, a, a^2, ..., a^k, equal to (a^(k+1) - 1)/(a - 1), which is bounded by a constant over 1 - a when |a| < 1.

known.name: Recurrence relations
known.gloss: An equation that defines each term of a sequence from earlier terms, solved by repeatedly substituting it into itself until the terms form a sum with a closed form or bound.

known.name: Mathematical induction and proof by contradiction
known.gloss: Proof techniques in which a statement is established for all integers by proving a base case and an inductive step, or in which an assumption is refuted by deriving a contradiction.

known.name: Sets, Cartesian products and lexicographic order
known.gloss: Finite sets with their intersections, Cartesian products of index sets whose tuples are compared first by the leftmost coordinate, and the indicator vector that records membership of each element.

known.name: Permutations and permutation matrices
known.gloss: A permutation is a bijection of a finite set onto itself, written in cycle notation, and its permutation matrix moves each coordinate to its image.

known.name: Binomial coefficients and counting subsets
known.gloss: The number of k-element subsets of an n-element set, written binom(n, k), together with the simple counting arguments that compute and bound such numbers.

known.name: Polar form, Euler's formula and roots of unity
known.gloss: Every complex number of modulus r can be written as r e^(i theta) = r(cos theta + i sin theta), and the n-th roots of unity are the n complex numbers e^(2 pi i j/n) for j = 0, ..., n-1.

known.name: Matrix rank and Gaussian elimination
known.gloss: The rank of a matrix is the dimension of its column space, computed by Gaussian elimination with elementary row operations, and a square matrix is invertible exactly when its rank equals its size.

known.name: Directed graphs
aliases: sources and sinks of a digraph
known.gloss: A directed graph consists of vertices joined by edges with a direction, where a source has no incoming edges, a sink has no outgoing edges, and a path follows edges in their directions.

known.name: Worst-case time complexity of Turing machines
known.gloss: The worst-case running time of a Turing machine is the maximum number of steps it takes on any input of length n, and a time bound is a function of n bounding this count.

known.name: Sorting, stability and radix sort
known.gloss: Sorting arranges records by key, a sort is stable when records with equal keys keep their original order, and radix sort sorts digit by digit using stable passes.

known.name: Schoolbook multiplication and long division
known.gloss: The digit-by-digit algorithms for multiplying and dividing integers, which take quadratic time in the number of digits.
